notes: Splits the growth-data privacy marker into two rule families and moves the privacy filter from a deployment env var to an organization-level setting. (1) privacy_filtered_rows previously conflated PII removals with page-identity URL-rule removals, so with filtering off a URL-rule removal was still stamped as a privacy filter. It is now split: pii_filtered_rows (email/phone/long-digit/token/control-char/over-long, controlled by the org switch) and url_rejected_rows (non-whitelisted query params, @ or token in the path — always applied). privacy_filtered_rows is retained as a read-only legacy marker: old snapshots keep it and are still treated as incomplete; nothing is rewritten. (2) The switch is now OrganizationServiceSettings.privacyFilter, a top-level field (like networkMode), stored inside the existing encrypted settings blob with no SQL migration. It is deliberately NOT placed under values: an unknown values sub-key is rejected by the previous release's validateSettings, which would break that organization's settings reads (effective(), and therefore growth collection, checks, compare and visibility) after a rollback; a top-level field is ignored by the previous release, so rollback to v0.2.20 is safe. Resolution order is RUNTIME_GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER (organization) -> GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER (deployment default) -> strict. There is no organization default: an unset organization falls back to the deployment default, so a deployment that currently relies on GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER=off keeps its behaviour after upgrade. The organization admin sets it under 系统设置 -> 组织服务配置 -> 运行参数; GET /settings/organization returns the resolved effective value as runtimeOverrides.privacyFilter and PUT /settings/organization/runtime accepts a top-level privacyFilter (the platform runtime route rejects that key). Collection receives it via the job env plus a withRuntimeEnvironment wrap in tenantGrowthRunner; the read paths (/growth, /growth/synthesis, /growth-opportunities, /agent/growth) resolve it per organization and pass it into loadGrowthInsights so already-stored data is not re-filtered with the wrong mode. /privacy and /google-data still disclose according to the deployment default and now note that organizations can adjust it. Local verification: three-package typecheck, pnpm --filter api test (1417 passed / 34 skipped), web production build, and a browser regression (desktop 1440 / mobile 375, no overflow, control visible, initial value = resolved effective setting, save submits privacyFilter). No SQL migration and no schema change. Rollback to v0.2.20 is compatible and is the declared rollback target.
